จุดตั้งต้นของสถานที่นี้อยู่ที่วัดเสนานุช: This place began at Wat Sena Nuch Rangsan, formerly known by local residents as “Wat Mai Kamphaeng.” The temple register records its establishment in B.E. 2390 (1847), while local sources say it was built during the reign of King Rama III by Phraya Sena Nuchit (Nuch), governor of Takuapa.
ในเวลานั้นตะกั่วป่าเป็นเมืองท่าชายฝั่งอั: At that time, Takuapa was an Andaman coastal port linking trade and tin resources. Various groups, especially workers and Chinese merchants, settled here, forming a market district and Chinese culture. The temple's Chinese-influenced ordination hall is therefore evidence of a multicultural town. For the museum seen today, no publicly available evidence identifies the year it was established or its direct founder.
No establishment year for the museum has been found; evidence shows its use in the old-town context before 2018 (B.E. 2561).
ระหว่างทาง วัดเสนานุชรังสรรค์ยังทำหน้าที: Over time, Wat Sena Nuch Rangsan has remained a religious site and community space. Meanwhile, Takuapa changed from a centre of tin mining and trade into a historic town preserving its heritage. Academic sources describe Takuapa Community Museum as a two-storey building displaying household items, equipment, and rare objects reflecting local life, including traces of the mining era.
อุโบสถวัดได้รับการขึ้นทะเบียนเป็นโบราณสถ: The temple's ordination hall is registered as an ancient monument by the Fine Arts Department, but the sources verifiable this time do not clearly state the registration year. No evidence has been found that the museum building was abandoned, underwent major restoration, or was directly affected by the 2004 tsunami (B.E. 2547), so no conclusion is made beyond the evidence.
หลักฐานร่วมสมัยเรียกพื้นที่นี้ทั้ง “พิพิ: Contemporary sources call this place both “Takuapa Community Museum” and “Takuapa House Museum.” It is presented in the context of the old-town cultural street, displaying photographs, artefacts, and community stories alongside Sino-Portuguese buildings and old temples. Its role is therefore more that of a place for learning about the town's memories than a large museum with full visitor services.

พิพิธภัณฑ์ชุมชนตะกั่วป่าเป็นอาคารสองชั้น: Takuapa Community Museum is a two-storey building inside Wat Sena Nuch Rangsan. It collects household items and equipment reflecting life in Takuapa, including objects from the mining era. Wat Sena Nuch Rangsan was built by Phraya Sena Nuchit (Nuch), and its ordination hall shows Chinese architectural influence.
